title: Hosted model performance bar (catalog launch requirements) v1
author: Ethan Park
body:
# Summary
This standard sets the minimum performance and reliability bar that any model must clear before it is added to the Hosted API catalog.

# Scope
Covers: chat/completions models served through the Hosted API, OpenAI-compatible routes included.
Excludes: one-off private customer builds (see Private Deployments standards).

# Owners
- Standard owner: Serving Runtime
- Enforcement: Release Engineering + SRE

# Benchmark methodology (required)
Use the `perf-canary` harness with these settings:
- Hardware class: `A100-80GB` (default); add a second class only if Product requests it
- Context sizes: 2k, 8k
- Workload: prompt-length mix taken from the top-10 Hosted API routes
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32
- Streaming: on

Required artifacts:
- Perf suite run IDs
- Raw logs attached to this Confluence page or linked from Drive
- Summary table with p50/p95 TTFT and tokens/sec

# Minimum bar for launch
The *candidate default config* must satisfy every item below.

## Latency
- TTFT p50 <= 1.5s (2k context)
- TTFT p95 <= 3.0s (2k context)
- TTFT p95 <= 5.0s (8k context)

## Throughput
- Sustained output tokens/sec per GPU >= family baseline minus 10%
- Continuous batching stays enabled; any exception needs a written reason and Runtime signoff

## Stability
- No crash loops during a 32-concurrency soak test (30 minutes)
- Error rate <= 0.5% for 2k and 8k tests
- No upward memory trend during soak (KV cache leak check)

# Launch decision and signoff
Signoffs are recorded as links/comments on the model intake Linear ticket:
- Serving Runtime: performance and stability
- SRE: capacity and readiness
- Release Engineering: rollout plan in place (see Platform runbook)

# If the model fails the bar
- If only TTFT fails and lowering default max_tokens fixes it, propose adjusted defaults and re-run the suite.
- If throughput is short, try quantization profiles and kernel flags; a degraded model ships only with Product signoff and a note in the docs.

# Related pages
- Model launch evaluation gates (Applied ML and Evals)
- Quant profile requirements for catalog (Applied ML and Evals)
- Hosted model rollout and fallback runbook (Eng Platform)
